According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple has several new features in the works for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 that should appeal more to health-conscious users. The company is also reportedly testing two finishes for the rumored ceramic version.

New Health Feature Upgrades

If you've been underwhelmed by the Apple Watch as a fitness tracker, these two major health feature upgrades should pique your interest. The two new features are: all-day heart rate tracking, and a completely redesigned app interface that makes it easier to extract useful information from your health data. Here's Gurman's description of the new app:

As a current WHOOP user, I'll say that the main thing that has kept me using it is that the WHOOP app makes it much easier to take useful information from my health data. It shows me all the factors contributing to why my sleep or recovery might be poor, whereas with the Apple Watch, it feels like the only thing that matters is your Activity rings. If Apple makes meaningful progress here, I'll be quite happy.

A key part of making the Apple Watch data experience richer is having more data. Apple is reportedly testing allowing the heart rate sensor to record continuously throughout the day, rather than only during workouts or at random times.

Two New Finishes

We've previously heard that Apple is considering ceramic for the Apple Watch Series 12, and Gurman now reports that there will be two color options: the traditional white, as well as a dark gray. There will also be "several new band colors and combinations" at launch.

Future Redesign

The current Apple Watch design language dates back to 2024 with the Apple Watch Series 10. That was a relatively modest change, with the company making the watch thinner at the cost of slightly larger bezels. According to Bloomberg, we may see a new Apple Watch design next year with the Series 11, though it's also possible it could slip to the Series 12:

I'm really looking forward to seeing what Apple comes up with next. They seem to have hit the ceiling of the rounded design language, so maybe we'll see a completely new form factor. Hopefully it doesn't impact backward compatibility with older bands.
